question:
How should modules be organized so that the software stays easy to maintain, and how can an existing badly structured program be improved without its users noticing any difference?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
[JEV filter] kept 15 of 15 guidelines (JEV 'lenient' score > 0.5)

# Guidelines
- Apply separation of concerns (SoC): identify and separate each distinct concern so the designer can focus on it in isolation. This is the foundational technique for effective ordering of design thoughts and a prerequisite for maintainability. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Separation of Concerns and Modularization in Software Design.md; root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Decision-Making Methods.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Use modularization (decomposition/refinement) to structure large software as smaller, well-named components with well-defined interfaces. [SWEBOK excerpt c5b822b2598e36a487ca]. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Separation of Concerns and Modularization in Software Design.md; root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Component Modularization and Single Responsibility Principle.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Assign each module a single responsibility. [SWEBOK excerpt 80f8229c668ac2ce83bd], as advocated by David Parnas, so that each module has one clear reason to change. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Component Modularization and Single Responsibility Principle.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Maximize cohesion within each module: organize [SWEBOK excerpt 80b67afc3c7f9d0fe564] so that the elements inside a module are strongly associated with one another. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Minimize coupling between modules: coupling is a measure of interdependence among modules, and [SWEBOK excerpt bc61089ce32a9b8024cd] so that changes in one module minimally affect others. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Apply encapsulation (information hiding): build upon abstraction and modularization so that non-essential [SWEBOK excerpt f0946ae00d8387954787]. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Separate interface from implementation: define each component by its public interfaces accessible to clients and isolate usage of the component from the details of how it is built. This is a direct application of information hiding. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Apply abstraction: focus [SWEBOK excerpt 3119e8792835caa7ca05] ignore the rest, so that essential properties common to superficially different entities can be identified and design complexity is managed. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Decision-Making Methods.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Strive for uniformity across modules: apply a principle of consistency so that common solutions address common or recurring problems, making the codebase more predictable and easier to maintain. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Use top-down decomposition (structured design): identify major software functions and elaborate them in a top-down manner, producing a hierarchy of modules where each level refines the one above. (source: root/Software Design Methodologies and Approaches/Design Strategies and Structured Approaches/Structured Design and Top-Down Function Decomposition.md; root/Software Design Methodologies and Approaches/Design Strategies and Structured Approaches/Design Strategies and Function-Oriented Methods.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Record design rationale — including prior assumptions, alternatives considered, and trade-offs analyzed — because reasons obvious to the current team can be opaque to future maintainers. Capturing rationale enhances long-term maintainability. (source: root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Improve a badly structured program through refactoring: reorganize the program without changing its observable behavior. Refactoring improves internal structure and maintainability while users experience no functional difference. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Use refactoring continuously (especially in Agile/CI contexts) to reduce technical debt before and after code changes. Continuous refactoring manages growing complexity while improving developer productivity. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Apply reverse engineering as a precursor to restructuring a legacy system: analyze the [SWEBOK excerpt 2914be4e220b25e4536a], creating representations at higher levels of abstraction that expose structural problems. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.79]
- Document the software design through a Software Design Description (SDD) that encompasses the refinement of [SWEBOK excerpt 29cc14a801ba59a99e92] — serving as a blueprint that supports future maintenance. (source: root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Architecture and Design Principles/Software Design Concepts and Documentation.md) [JEV 0.95]
